name: Monastero Santa Rosa
positioning: A restored 17th-century monastery on the cliff edge of Conca dei Marini, a fishing village on the Amalfi Coast, with terraced gardens, a spa and a pool that seems to float over the sea
best_for: Couples who want a secluded clifftop retreat with Mediterranean views
Travelers drawn to a historic monastery setting
Guests who want to hike or explore the coast by boat

facts.text: The hotel occupies a restored 17th-century monastery.
The monastery sits on the cliff edge of Conca dei Marini, overlooking the village.
Conca dei Marini is a fishing village a short 10-minute drive from Amalfi.
The hotel is three miles from Amalfi.
Below the cliff is the marina of Conca dei Marini, where fishermen have brought in their catch for centuries.
The hotel has clifftop Mediterranean views.
Guests can have a martini and play chess at the library and bar.
Il Refettorio serves local Campanian specialties.
Hikes in the region range from the Path of the Gods to the lesser-known Valley of the Ironworkers.
A private boat can be chartered for a half or full day to see the Amalfi Coast.
The hotel was named in Conde Nast Traveler's Readers' Choice Awards in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2025.

highlights.text: The pool seems to float over the sea.
There are four levels of terraced gardens to stroll.
The spa includes sauna and steam rooms, a hydro pool and a tepidarium.
The hotel still makes sfogliatelle pastries according to the nuns' original recipe.

considerations.text: The hotel is in the village of Conca dei Marini rather than in Amalfi town, a short 10-minute drive away.
WhataHotel notes that the hotel is reached by a winding coastal road.
